domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: Braintrust is explicitly a developer platform for evaluation and logging, and the talk introduces Loop as a new platform feature for automating eval optimization. The talk centers on a developer platform used by software builders at companies like Zapier, Notion, and Instacart. The discussion covers evaluation workflows and automated optimization of prompts, datasets, and scorers during development. The talk assumes familiarity with AI evals but is accessible to a general AI engineering conference audience. Recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair. All claims are directly sourced from the transcript with specific evidence anchors and character ranges.

summary: Ankur Goyal, founder and CEO of Braintrust, presents on the future of evals at the AI Engineer World's Fair in San Francisco. He opens by reflecting on Braintrust's nearly two-year journey working with companies like Zapier, Notion, Instacart, and Airtable. Adoption metrics are striking: the average organization signing up runs almost 13 evals per day, some customers exceed 3,000 evals daily, and the most advanced companies spend over two hours daily working through their evals in the product. Despite this sophistication, Goyal identifies a core limitation: the best current eval experience is simply a dashboard users look at and then manually decide what code or prompt changes to make. He frames this as about to change fundamentally. He introduces Loop, an agent built into Braintrust that automatically optimizes prompts all the way to complex agents, and also helps build better datasets and scorers. Loop became viable because Braintrust has run quarterly evals on frontier models for two years to assess their ability at improving prompts, datasets, and scorers; until recently models were not good enough. Goyal cites Claude 4 as a breakthrough, performing approximately six times better than the previous leading model. Loop is available now via a feature flag in Braintrust, defaults to Claude 4 but supports any model including OpenAI, Gemini, or custom LLMs. The UI shows suggested edits side by side, preserving the data-inspection workflow users value. An autonomous toggle lets Loop optimize without manual review. Goyal closes by calling for users to try Loop, give feedback, and notes Braintrust is hiring across UI, AI, and infrastructure.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Evals Adoption and Current Limitations
sections.summary: Goyal reflects on Braintrust's two-year journey, sharing adoption metrics: average orgs run 13 evals/day, some run 3,000+, advanced users spend 2+ hours daily. He identifies the core limitation: evals today are just a dashboard you look at and walk away from, then manually decide changes.

sections.title: Introducing Loop
sections.summary: Goyal introduces Loop, an agent built into Braintrust that automatically optimizes prompts, datasets, and scorers. It was enabled by quarterly evals on frontier models over two years; Claude 4 was a breakthrough performing approximately six times better than the previous leading model.

sections.title: Loop UI, Models, and Usage
sections.summary: Loop is available via a feature flag, defaults to Claude 4 but supports any model. The UI shows suggested edits side by side for data, scoring, and prompts. An autonomous toggle lets Loop optimize without manual review, which Goyal says works well.

sections.title: Recap and Call to Action
sections.summary: Goyal recaps that evals have been critical but manual, and predicts evals will be revolutionized by frontier models over the next year. He invites users to try Loop, give feedback, and notes Braintrust is hiring across UI, AI, and infrastructure.
